notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch (curl), no blocking, robots.txt allows crawling (Shopify storefront). Discovery: main nav has exactly one 'Clearance' top-level link (/collections/clearance) -- no other Clearance/Outlet/Final Sale/Last Chance link anywhere in header, footer, or the category mega-menus. Also fetched the full site collections.json (726 collections, paginated) and keyword-scanned for clear/outlet/sale/final/discontinu/last-chance. SALE VS CLEARANCE (the critical distinction): the collections.json scan surfaced many *-sale collections, but every one of them was excluded as a generic/temporary or vendor promotion, not clearance: 'sale' (16,998 products; og:title 'Save on The Best Home Furniture Brands!' -- a generic sitewide markdown page, not linked in nav, no clearance/outlet/permanent-markdown language anywhere on the page); 'rugs-for-sale' (8,009) and 'outdoor-dining-chairs' (og:title 'Outdoor Dining Chairs for Sale', 100) -- in both, 'for sale' is plain SEO phrasing meaning 'available for purchase' (the og:description carries no discount/markdown language at all), essentially aliasing the full category, not a clearance concept; the various brand-specific *-sale collections (bdi-*-sale, bernhardt-sale*, lexington-spring-sale, lexington-winter-sale, back-to-school-sale-1, hooker-holiday-sale, 20-off-sale) are vendor/seasonal promotional campaigns, several already at 0 products, none carrying clearance/outlet/final-sale/end-of-line language; 'hooker-non-clearance-items' explicitly self-labels as the opposite of clearance. None of these were ambiguous enough to warrant a MANUAL REVIEW flag -- each lacked any clearance/outlet/permanent-markdown signal and none is presented in the site's own taxonomy (nav, breadcrumb, or on-page copy) as clearance. QTY METHOD: Shopify collections.json 'products_count' proven inflated site-wide (established in prior Home-Decor pass); used the rendered utility-bar 'N products' header on the collection page instead (2067), vs. the inflated collections.json count of 2337.
